questions.prompt: I link the gallbladder to the main bile highway, and inside the little triangle that bears my surgeon's name, an artery hides that must be found before I am cut. Who am I?

I hang by a stalk beneath the brain, ruled from above, resting snug in a bony saddle. Who am I?
I am the largest solid organ in the abdomen, sitting mostly on the right, and I make bile. Who am I?
I am the liver lobe that hugs the great vein and drains straight into it through my own small veins. Who am I?
I hide deep behind the knee, easily bruised, and split in two just below it. Who am I?
I am a great bridge of white fibers linking the two hemispheres — cut me and the halves talk far less. Who am I?
I am the body's pump, about the size of a fist, and I never take a day off. Who am I?
I cap the kidneys with a cortex of three layers and a medulla that makes adrenaline. Who am I?
We are tiny air sacs in the lungs where oxygen enters the blood. Who are we?
I run down inside the backbone and connect the brain to the rest of the body. Who am I?
I am the widest gap in the base of the skull, where the brainstem quietly becomes the spinal cord. Who am I?
I lie flat in the middle of the front of the chest, and ribs join me through cartilage. Who am I?
I wrap around the neck of the leg's outer lower bone. A careless cast or crossed legs can leave the foot dropping. Who am I?
I am the lowest recess of the female peritoneal cavity when standing, lying between the uterus and the rectum. Who am I?
I am the windpipe, kept open by rings of cartilage so air can flow to the lungs. Who am I?
I sit under the liver and store the greenish fluid that helps digest fat. Who am I?
I lie behind the stomach with my head cradled by the C-loop of the bowel and my tail near the spleen; I have both exocrine and endocrine jobs. Who am I?
I drape from the stomach like an apron and wall off infection — the 'policeman' of the abdomen. Who am I?
I collect blood from the left gonad, then slip in front of the aorta to reach the great vein — squeeze me there and a nutcracker awaits. Who am I?
No muscle ever holds me, yet the whole body's weight passes down through me from the leg bone above. Who am I?
Cut me during thyroid surgery and the voice turns hoarse. I run close to an artery of the thyroid, though I am not that vessel. Who am I?
Below the inguinal ligament, beside the vein that shares my neighborhood, a loop of bowel can sneak through me — more often in women. What hernia am I?
I am the larger, weight-bearing bone of the leg below the knee, known as the shin bone. Who am I?
I run beneath the flexor retinaculum with nine tendons for company. Squeeze me, and your thumb, index, and middle finger tingle at night. Who am I?
Break the shaft of the arm's long bone and you may bruise me as I spiral around it — do so, and the wrist can no longer lift itself up. Who am I?
I sit where the great veins of the head and body meet the heart's right chamber, and my ancient rhythm sets the beat. Who am I?
I am a bony helmet that protects the brain. Who am I?
Before birth I link the pulmonary trunk to the aortic arch; after birth I close and leave a ligament behind. Who am I?
Of all the cranial nerves, I wander the farthest, from the brainstem down toward the gut. Who am I?
I carry urine, cross the pelvic brim over the iliac vessels, and hide under a uterine vessel like water under a bridge. Who am I?
We are a pair of bean-shaped filters that clean the blood and make urine. Who are we?
I bulge on the front of your upper arm when you bend your elbow. Who am I?
I am the body's largest lymphatic channel, born from a sac in the abdomen and emptying at the left venous angle. Who am I?
I curl around the neck of the forearm's outer bone like a question mark. Injure me, and the wrist and fingers can no longer straighten. Who am I?
Squeeze the space between collarbone and first rib, or between two neck muscles, and a whole bundle of vessels and nerves complains — what is this compression called?
